title: Robot Choir
subtitle: French house · a choir of vowels with no words
statement: Saw waves sung through moving vowel formants. The chords walk around the vowel circle, u, o, a, e, i; one robot voice sings the handshake.
intro: Somewhere in the machine, a choir learning to sing without words.

sections.name: Doors
sections.intent: Drums for the mix; the disco bass from bar 9.

sections.name: Verse
sections.intent: Electric piano and the bass; the choir enters on the off-beats.

sections.name: Chorus
sections.intent: The robot voice sings the handshake over held choir chords.
moves: Lead voice: G, D, G, B-flat on oo, ah, ee, oh.

sections.name: Choir Alone
sections.intent: Kick out. The choir holds long chords, the vowels turning slowly.

sections.name: Chorus II
sections.intent: Everything, with the voice an octave up for its second half.
sections.feeling: The loudest singing of the night so far.

sections.name: Exit
sections.intent: Drums and bass; drums alone for the last 8 bars.

layers.name: Kick
layers.description: A punchy 909-style kick tuned to G.

layers.name: Clap
layers.description: A clap on 2 and 4, darker than take 1.

instrument.name: Drum kit
instrument.description: clap, hat, kick, open, ride, rim, shaker

layers.name: Hats
layers.description: Metallic hats from six band-limited square oscillators (the 808 recipe): short closed ticks and off-beat open hats, almost no noise.
layers.purpose: The tick of the groove, kept small.

instrument.name: Drum kit
instrument.description: clap, hat, kick, open, ride, rim, shaker

layers.name: Robot choir
layers.description: Saw-wave chords sung through four moving vowel formants. Each chord's vowels walk the circle u → o → a → e → i.
layers.math: formants interpolate between vowel targets (F1–F4) along each chord's path

instrument.name: Robot Choir
instrument.description: Saw chord through four moving vowel formants, like a vocoder with no words.

layers.name: Disco bass
layers.description: Octave disco bass with passing sevenths and fifths: saw and square into a snappy ladder. Since take 3 it rides above the warm bass, high-passed at 220 Hz: the bite and the talk, not the weight.

instrument.name: Mono Synth
instrument.description: Saw, square and sub oscillators, glide, vibrato and an enveloped resonant filter.

layers.name: Electric piano
layers.description: FM electric piano comping a syncopated house rhythm.

instrument.name: FM Electric Piano
instrument.description: Two-operator FM: a warm 1:1 body and a ratio-14 tine strike, with stereo tremolo.

layers.name: Robot voice
layers.description: One sung line on vowels only: the handshake (G, D, G, B-flat) on oo, ah, ee, oh, then an answer falling back to D. In Chorus II it steps aside for the real voice, then returns an octave up, still wordless.

instrument.name: Robot Choir
instrument.description: Saw chord through four moving vowel formants, like a vocoder with no words.

layers.name: Air choir
layers.description: A synth choir: four drifting, vibrato-ed saw singers per note through five choir formants, each chord walking its own vowels. No breath noise.
layers.purpose: An octave of human-shaped voices above the robots for the loudest chorus.

instrument.name: Synth Choir
instrument.description: An ensemble of drifting, vibrato-ed saws per note through five choir formants; tones, no noise.

layers.name: Finger bass
layers.description: An electric bass played with the fingers: a plucked string built from its harmonics, highs dying first.
layers.purpose: The warm foundation: it owns everything below about 250 Hz.

instrument.name: Finger Bass
instrument.description: A plucked string from its harmonics: pluck and pickup position shape the tone, highs decay first, then tape warmth.

instrument.name: Transition FX
instrument.description: Noise risers, downlifters, impacts, crashes, reversed crashes and sub drops.

layers.name: Voice (learning)
layers.description: The robot voice's melody, now with words, still hard-tuned and ring-modulated: a voice that has just been given consonants.

instrument.name: Electric Bat voice
instrument.description: The project's singing synthesizer: lyrics to phonemes, a human performance, autotune, then production.

layers.name: Voice (learned)
layers.description: The same melody sung human, with doubles: the voice has learned, and the robot choir above it keeps singing only vowels.

instrument.name: Electric Bat voice
instrument.description: The project's singing synthesizer: lyrics to phonemes, a human performance, autotune, then production.

layers.name: Robots
layers.description: A speech chip doubling the wordless robot voice, holograms of each chord while the choir is alone, and small servo moves at the ends of the verse phrases.

instrument.name: Robot rack
instrument.description: Machines from the batsynth robot library (servos, droids, modems, coils, turbines, alarms, clocks).

lanes.name: tension (plan)
lanes.description: How tense each section is meant to feel.

annotations.text: The choir starts on the off-beats.
The robot voice sings the handshake.

lyrics.text: now I can say your name.
I don't know what I'm made of,
but I know what I want to say,

lyrics_take4.text: Oo, ah, ee, oh, I only had the vowels, oh.
Then you gave me consonants, little edges, now
I can say the word for light, say the word for you.
Every question starts with a breath and ends with teeth.
Oo, ah, ee, oh, I can talk, I can say it loud.
Say a word for what I am: there's no word for that.
So I'll sing the vowels back: oo, ah, ee, oh, oh.
Now I can say the only word I needed: you.
